validated_results.title: Modifiable risk factors for subsequent lethal prostate cancer among men with an initially negative prostate biopsy.
validated_results.reason: This prospective cohort study evaluates the association between alcohol consumption and incident prostate cancer risk among men with an initial negative biopsy.

extraction.population: Health Professionals Follow-up Study (HPFS) participants with an initial negative prostate biopsy

sample_size.excerpt: As a result, 10,396 men had a prostate biopsy with negative results were included in the current study.

cases.excerpt: With 1851 prostate cancer cases (168 lethal) diagnosed over 23 years of follow-up, the 20-year risk of any prostate cancer diagnosis was 18.5% (95% CI: 17.7–19.3).

design.excerpt: This study aimed to address both questions and assess 16 potential risk factors for prostate cancer among men with an initial negative prostate biopsy in a large prospective cohort in the U.S.

exposure_measurement.excerpt: Dietary and nutrient intakes were assessed by a validated food frequency questionnaire [ 24 ] at baseline in 1986 and every 4 years thereafter, which served to estimate total energy intake for energy adjustment and included intakes of tomato sauce, coffee, dairy products, calcium, processed meat, red meat, fish, and alcohol.

extraction.p_value_method: two-sided Wald test from effect and 95% CI on the log scale
